title: Mathlib v4.30 source proposition Int.modEq_neg
statement: The proposition declared as `Int.modEq_neg` in the pinned Mathlib v4.30 source.

formal.statement: ∀ {n a b : ℤ}, a ≡ b [ZMOD -n] ↔ a ≡ b [ZMOD n]

Both are pinned by the same test, so dropping either half fails it rather than quietly halving the claim. Neither carries an `Int.lt Int.zero` premise, matching the row's unrestricted quantification.

notes:
THE REASON THIS ROW CLOSED WHILE THIRTEEN SIBLINGS DID NOT is worth recording. Every congruence lemma in `modeq.rs` is proved only under `0 < n`, because the sole bound on `emod`'s magnitude, `emod_lt_of_pos`, needs a positive divisor; the ml430 rows carry no such hypothesis. `Int.emod_neg` needs NO positivity at all -- it is a constructor case split, not an inequality argument -- which is precisely why it reaches an unrestricted statement where the existing machinery cannot. It is also the intended lever for several of the remaining rows, since it folds the n < 0 case back onto the positive bridge; what is still missing for those is a natAbs-based generalisation of `emod_lt_of_pos`, flagged as not yet built in `int_prelude/division.rs`'s own header.

The two halves are recorded as one fact because the ledger row is one biconditional. Splitting them into two facts would let half the row read as closed.
